options.label: Current plan: egui chat home in 4 days, clap REPL
options.burden: low toolchain, high dual-UI debt later
options.why: egui can show bubbles; it cannot become Codex TUI. CLI stays a form/REPL. A later ratatui would duplicate chat.rs.

options.label: Rust core + ratatui TUI as the product; egui stays Compare/Agents
options.burden: one language, one extra crate family (ratatui/crossterm)
options.why: Codex is the existence proof that a Rust TUI can be the daily driver. Desktop polish stays below Claude.app; interaction quality can match.

options.label: Rust core + OpenCode/Tauri or SolidJS as the chat shell
options.burden: Bun/Node + Rust, two CI worlds, license PORT of a moving target
options.why: Fastest visual desktop. Raises burden, which is the opposite of 'Rust to reduce load'. TUI would still be missing unless also adopted.

options.label: egui chat AND ratatui TUI as separate implementations
options.burden: rule 5 violation: two composers, two session lists
options.why: Looks complete, drifts immediately. Codex does not do this: TUI and desktop share app-server.

because: Codex, the quality bar named by the user, is a Rust ratatui TUI. Staying Rust is how you copy that bar rather than fight it.
Rust already carries process, adapters, policy, verify, mission. Adding Bun/Tauri increases burden, which the user asked to reduce.
egui is the wrong primary chat surface: no TUI, weak selection/copy, and a second implementation if a TUI is added later.
Claude.app visual polish is not available to port. Claiming it in four days is a plan failure, same class as 'merge after tests' ignoring untracked files.
/compare on MissionRunner is the one part of the current plan that is correctly scoped.
verdict.what_egui_is_for: Compare, Constellation, Agent board, Policy inspector — a companion, not the composer.
integrator_dependency_requests: tui-textarea or equivalent composer (MIT/Apache; record in upstream-sources.toml if PORT)
